title: Certification Inspector
description:
Department: Vertical Transportation

Lerch Bates is seeking a Certification Inspector to join our NYC Vertical Transportation team. In this role, you will perform inspections of elevators, escalators, and related conveyance systems to verify compliance with applicable codes, regulations, and safety standards. Your expertise will play a critical role in helping building owners, contractors, property managers, and regulatory agencies ensure the safe operation of vertical transportation equipment.

As a Certification Inspector, you will conduct inspections of new and existing equipment, evaluate compliance with applicable codes and standards, investigate deficiencies, and prepare detailed inspection reports. You will serve as a trusted technical resource while working closely with building owners, contractors, architects, code officials, and other stakeholders throughout the inspection process.

Become an Employee-Owner

One of the biggest advantages of working at Lerch Bates is that we are 100% employee-owned through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP).

Unlike many companies that offer only a salary and retirement plan, eligible employees receive company-funded ESOP shares at no cost to them as part of their long-term retirement benefits.

As Lerch Bates grows, employee-owners share in the company's success. For many employees, the ESOP becomes one of the most valuable financial benefits of their career by helping build meaningful long-term wealth in addition to their salary and traditional 401(k).

When you join Lerch Bates, you are not just building better buildings. You also have the opportunity to build your financial future alongside the company's success.

About Lerch Bates:

Lerch Bates (LB) is a global technical consulting firm focused on improving how buildings perform for owners, designers, and the people who use them every day. For more than 75 years we’ve partnered on some of the world’s most complex and high-profile projects. Today we provide Total Building Performance expertise that integrates Building Science and Building Flow into a unified delivery model.

Our work spans design, construction, investigation, repair, rehabilitation, management, and modernization with one consistent goal: helping clients make confident, well-informed decisions in an increasingly complex built environment.

We are 100% employee-owned through our ESOP. That means when the company succeeds, our employee-owners share in that success. It's more than a retirement benefit—it's an ownership mindset backed by the opportunity to build long-term financial value while helping shape the future of the company.

What You’ll Do:

The duties listed below are intended only as illustrations of the various types of work that may be performed in this position. They are not intended to prescribe or restrict the assignments that management may make.

Inspections & Compliance

  • Perform inspections of new and existing elevators, escalators, moving walks, and other lifting equipment in residential, commercial, and industrial buildings.
  • Evaluate equipment and installations for compliance with applicable building codes, elevator safety codes, and regulatory requirements.
  • Determine compliance or non-compliance with applicable standards and document findings accordingly.
  • Verify that inspections are performed in accordance with Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements and applicable certification standards.
  • Conduct follow-up inspections to verify corrective actions and code compliance.

Technical Evaluation & Reporting

  • Investigate potential code violations, safety concerns, and equipment deficiencies.
  • Prepare complete, accurate, and timely inspection reports for clients, building owners, and regulatory agencies.
  • Document inspection findings, observations, deficiencies, and recommendations in accordance with company and regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain inspection records and submit required documentation by established deadlines.
  • Ensure all reports meet Lerch Bates quality standards and regulatory expectations.

Client & Stakeholder Support

  • Interpret and explain applicable codes, regulations, standards, and inspection requirements to clients, contractors, property owners, architects, building management personnel, and code authorities.
  • Serve as a trusted technical resource during inspections and certification activities.
  • Maintain professional communication with clients and project stakeholders throughout the inspection process.
  • Support positive client relationships through responsive service and technical expertise.

Safety & Professional Standards

  • Follow established company procedures, processes, forms, and quality standards.
  • Comply with all applicable safety regulations and industry best practices.
  • Utilize required personal protective equipment (PPE) while performing field inspections and site visits.
  • Maintain current knowledge of industry codes, technologies, equipment, and regulatory requirements.
  • Perform additional duties and special projects as assigned.

What You’ll Bring:

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Current Qualified Elevator Inspector (QEI) certification required.
  • New York City Department of Buildings Elevator Agency Inspector or Director License required.
  • New York State Department of Labor Elevator Inspector License required.
  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
  • 10+ years of elevator industry experience preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience conducting inspections, maintenance evaluations, audits, field supervision, or related activities preferred.
  • Thorough knowledge of ASME elevator codes, industry regulations, standards, and safety requirements.
  • Strong understanding of elevator, escalator, and vertical transportation systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated critical thinking, problem-solving, and analytical abilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Professional demeanor with the ability to interact effectively with clients, contractors, code officials, and building stakeholders.
  • Ability to travel throughout the region on a regular basis.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain any additional jurisdictional certifications or licenses required to perform inspections.

Why Work with Lerch Bates?

  • Competitive base salary of $65 - $5 per hour, based on experience, qualifications, and location
  • Annual performance-based bonus opportunity, with target incentive levels varying by position and based on individual and company performance.
  • 100% Employee-Owned ESOP (company-funded retirement benefit that allows eligible employees to share in the company's long-term success)
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid time off (starting at 17 days annually)
  • 10 paid holidays
  • 401(k) with 6% employer match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Professional development and tuition reimbursement
  • Employee assistance and wellness programs

Core Values

Ownership • Community • Integrity • Respect • Optimism

Working Environment:

This position is performed in a combination of office, client, and field environments. Work regularly takes place in occupied buildings, active construction sites, mechanical rooms, elevator machine rooms, elevator pits, hoistways, and other vertical transportation spaces.

Travel throughout the assigned service area is required.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Physical Demands:

This position requires frequent standing, walking, climbing stairs and ladders, bending, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and navigating active construction sites and existing buildings.

Employees may be required to work at heights, access elevator machine rooms, elevator pits, hoistways, rooftops, and other confined spaces while wearing appropriate PPE. The position may require lifting or carrying equipment weighing up to 40 pounds.

Travel by automobile and occasional air travel may be required.

Mental Demands:

This position requires strong analytical, organizational, and technical problem-solving skills. Employees must interpret technical drawings, specifications, maintenance records, inspection reports, and applicable codes and standards while exercising sound professional judgment.

The role requires managing multiple projects, coordinating with clients and contractors, preparing technical reports, and communicating complex technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a pre-employment background check and drug test. The drug test includes screening for marijuana, regardless of state or local laws permitting its use. A conditional offer of employment will be rescinded if a candidate fails either the background check or the drug test. This requirement is mandated by federal regulations applicable to our government contracting obligations.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Director of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
description:

We’re entering an exciting next stage in our AI journey and are looking for a Director of Artificial Intelligence to build and lead our enterprise AI capability. What You’ll Do

You'll have the opportunity to shape the team, strategy, operating model, technology choices, governance, and portfolio that define how AI creates value across our global organization.

title: Process Operator - 3rd shift
description:
Job purpose

The Process Operator is responsible for ensuring the efficient, safe, and compliant operation of production equipment within the production line. This role serves as a technical expert on the line, monitoring critical parameters to guarantee product quality and food safety while actively identifying opportunities to minimize waste. The ideal candidate possesses strong mechanical aptitude, a commitment to safety, and a focus on operational efficiency through waste reduction.

Duties and responsibilities

1. Safety & Compliance

  • Strictly adhere to all plant safety regulations, including the consistent wearing of required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and rigorous application of Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures.
  • Actively identify, report, and assist in mitigating safety hazards or non-compliance issues within the process area to maintain a zero-incident workplace.
  • Promote a proactive culture of safety by modeling best practices

2. Quality Control

  • Continuously monitor and validate critical process parameters—such as moisture levels, oil absorption, temperature, Free Fatty Acids (FFAs), and dough consistency—to ensure finished products meet internal and regulatory specifications.
  • Perform regular quality checks and document results for key metrics, including:
  • Water temperature
  • Mixing time
  • Dough moisture
  • Moisture levels after oven/stabilizer
  • Oil absorption (for fried products)
  • Final product texture (e.g., Takis texture)

Collaborate closely with the Quality Assurance (QA) department to address non-conformances immediately and implement effective corrective actions to prevent product waste.

Ensure full compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) principles, and FDA regulations at all times.

3. Equipment Operation & Maintenance

  • Safely operate and monitor all processing equipment—including mixers, ovens, fryers, and stabilizers—in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Perform basic troubleshooting and make precise adjustments to machinery to minimize downtime, reduce scrap, and maintain product flow.
  • Promptly report equipment malfunctions or unusual wear to the maintenance team and production supervisors.

4. Process Improvement & Documentation

  • Accurately record all production data, equipment settings, and process deviations in the GB connected.
  • Actively support 5S initiatives to ensure work areas remain clean, organized, and efficient, which directly contributes to waste reduction.
  • Identify opportunities for process optimization (e.g., reducing ingredient waste, minimizing product giveaways, improving efficiency) and contribute ideas to continuous improvement projects.
  • Maintain clear and effective communication by participating in production loops, including shift handovers.

5. Leadership & Collaboration

  • Guide on daily tasks and managing complex operational scenarios, with an emphasis on efficiency and waste reduction.
  • Work cross-functionally with Production Supervisors, QA, and Maintenance teams to resolve issues quickly and meet daily production targets without sacrificing quality or creating excess waste.
  • Serve as a subject-matter expert (SME) for the process area, providing insight and guidance during audits, training sessions, and process changes.

title: Quality Assurance Engineer
description:
Quality Assurance Engineer

Job Overview

PacSci EMC is seeking a Quality Assurance Engineer to provide customer- and program-focused quality leadership across assigned aerospace and defense programs. This role serves as a key quality interface with customers and internal program teams while maintaining end-to-end ownership of quality issues that may extend into manufacturing and the supplier base.

Essential Functions

• Own quality performance for assigned customer and program portfolios, serving as a primary quality interface with customers and aerospace/defense prime contractors.

• Review proposals, statements of work, customer requirements, and related program documentation to help ensure alignment with design intent, quality requirements, regulatory requirements, and contractual commitments.

• Partner closely with Program Management and cross-functional teams including Engineering, Operations, Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, and Supplier Quality to identify, assess, and resolve quality risks.

• Maintain end-to-end ownership of quality issues across customer, manufacturing, and supplier boundaries; coordinate the appropriate resources and drive issues through effective resolution.

• Support first article readiness and execution, including AS9102/FAI requirements, and help ensure supplier quality requirements and flow-downs are understood and properly implemented.

• Lead and support root cause investigation and corrective/preventive action using structured methodologies such as 5 Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, CAPA, 8D, Apollo, or other appropriate problem-solving methods.

• Support manufacturing process validation, control plans, inspection instructions, quality records, and other quality-system documentation required to demonstrate process and product compliance.

• Analyze production and quality data to identify trends, systemic issues, and improvement opportunities, and use data to support sound technical and business decisions.

• Participate in customer and program reviews as the quality and compliance voice for assigned programs, communicating risks, status, corrective actions, and quality performance clearly and professionally.

• Exercise independent judgment and ownership in making quality decisions that may have significant customer, program, compliance, and financial impact; escalate appropriately when additional support or authority is required.

• Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma, and other appropriate quality tools and methodologies.

• Build effective working relationships across functions and levels of the organization, influencing outcomes without direct authority and fostering a team-first approach to problem solving.

Education and Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline preferred; equivalent directly relevant quality engineering experience will be considered.

• Three or more years of hands-on Quality Engineering experience required; five or more years preferred.

• Aerospace and defense quality experience strongly preferred. Experience in other highly regulated manufacturing environments, particularly medical device or automotive, may also be considered.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Demonstrated experience supporting customer- or program-facing quality activities, including direct interaction with customers and cross-functional program teams.

• Strong working knowledge of manufacturing process validation, control plans, inspection methods, quality records, and corrective action processes.

• Experience with structured root cause and corrective action methods; ability to select and apply the appropriate method based on the problem.

• Working knowledge of AS9100 strongly preferred; strong ISO 9001 experience may be considered where it demonstrates transferable quality-system capability.

• Experience with AS9102 / First Article Inspection strongly preferred.

• Working knowledge of GD&T, FMEA, process capability/Cpk, and related quality engineering tools preferred.

• Lean and/or Six Sigma experience preferred.

• Ability to interpret technical requirements and communicate quality and compliance expectations across Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, suppliers, and customers.

• Strong analytical judgment, ownership, curiosity, and decision-making capability, including the confidence to make consequential decisions with appropriate escalation.

• Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills; able to influence different personalities and functions without direct authority.

• Positive, team-oriented, and coachable approach with a willingness to ask for help, challenge assumptions constructively, and remain engaged until issues are resolved.

• No specific ERP, statistical analysis, or quality software package is required for consideration.

Work Environment and Travel

• This position is 100% onsite.

• Typical schedule is Monday through Friday with reasonable flexibility in start time based on business and leadership alignment. Mission and customer needs may occasionally require additional hours.

• Travel is expected to be minimal, generally approximately 5% or less.

Why Join PacSci EMC

• Join a growing aerospace and defense business with significant customer demand and long-term opportunity.

• Gain exposure to the specialized energetics market and work directly with major aerospace and defense customers.

• Develop broad quality expertise through exposure to Customer/Program, Manufacturing, and Supplier Quality.

• Work in a highly visible role with meaningful program ownership and interaction across multiple levels of the organization.

• Build experience that can support progression into more senior Quality Engineering and future leadership opportunities.

Export Control Requirement

Due to U.S. Government contract requirements applicable to this position, only U.S. citizens are eligible for employment in this role.

title: Freight Conductor - Beauharnois, QC
description:
Please read entire posting before applying to this position.

A Freight Conductor's primary responsibility is to safely coordinate train crews on a freight train, place rail cars to facilitate loading and unloading, and makeup/breakdown trains in a rail yard, customer facility or similar locations. To know more of what a day-in-the-life looks like for a conductor, please click to see a video here.

New hire conductors will be eligible to receive retention bonuses upon completion of their first and second year of service from date of promotion/qualification. The minimum amount to expect is $3000 after 1 year, and $2000 after year 2, but may be greater based on work location and is subject to the terms of the applicable direct hire agreement.

Note: You must pass a drug test (hair follicle and urine), medical exam, and background check to be hired into this role.

Must live within or be willing to relocate within 50 miles of posted location. Relocation assistance is not offered for this position.

Depending in the business need, you may be placed in a pipeline during the hiring process. If you are selected for the position, more information about the pipeline possibility will be discussed.

Primary Activities and Responsibilities

  • Ensure compliance with all railroad and safety rules, Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) regulations, railroad signals, and train orders
  • Be able to safely perform all job responsibilities
  • Inspect all equipment on cars prior to departures
  • Receive and transmit information by radio and telephone
  • Read and understand bulletins, work orders, and switch lists
  • Assist with the coupling and uncoupling of cars, operate switches, and make minor repairs to railcars, including replacing heavy couplings or air brake hoses
  • Work with customers to ensure accurate movement and placement of cars; delivers excellent customer service by identifying customer needs and meeting or exceeding expectations
  • Maintain awareness of surrounding area and suspicious activity to ensure rail safety
  • Operate locomotive equipment using remote control device
  • Comprehend color and/or hand signals and systems
  • Review instructions from yardmasters, dispatchers, and other transportation employees, and discuss with locomotive engineer
  • Miscellaneous activities and responsibilities as assigned by manager

Canada NMAD

  • Training rate while in Atlanta: $1,228.78 USD ($1,678.02 CAD) weekly
  • OJT Training Rate: $1,474.53 USD ($2,013.62 CAD) weekly
  • After OJT, guaranteed extra-board pay of $1,386.21 USD ($1,893.01 CAD) weekly
  • $82,555 USD ($112,737.11 CAD) average first year earnings including training. After training first year conductor average $96,725.00 USD ($132,087.66 CAD)

Canada Bonus

  • 1st year - $5,569.22 cash payment
  • 2nd year - $3,712.81 cash payment


Training

You are expected to attend four weeks of paid training at the Atlanta Training Center (ATC) in Atlanta, GA. Training includes a combination of classroom and computer-based learning, hands-on simulations, and physical competencies. New hires must maintain an 85% passing rate on quizzes and tests to remain in training. Failure to maintain the 85% average will result in new hires being released from the program, and their offer will be rescinded. CSX will provide a hotel room for the entire four weeks. New hires will receive a $20 per day meal allowance starting the first day of training. The REDI Cafe operated by Sodexo provides lunch options at a standardized cost of $7 plus tax on class days. Roundtrip mileage will be reimbursed at the IRS rate between the hiring location and Atlanta, as well as mileage between the training center and hotel. On-the-job training begins immediately following the successful completion of training at the ATC.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 18 years of age or older
  • One year of related experience
  • High School Diploma/GED/CAEC
  • Ability to read and comprehend all instructions including operating rules, bulletins, regulatory documents and other written communications
  • Proficient verbal and written communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • One or more years of outside work experience, e.g. construction, heavy equipment operations, farming, etc. (can be professional, personal, or volunteer experience)
  • Experience working in a safety sensitive environment

Job Requirements

  • Work safely to prevent on the job accidents and injuries
  • Must wear CSX approved protective equipment such as high-visibility vest, safety boots, hard hat, and hearing protection
  • Work hours may include a nonstandard workweek, overtime, and various shift work
  • Work hours are based on seniority, new hires primarily work on-call, nights, weekends, and holidays
  • Must be able to safely report to work within two hours of being notified to report
  • May be required to travel and be away from home terminal for 24 hours or longer
  • Work outdoors in varying weather conditions
  • Complete annual training and pass safety rules examinations
  • Federal regulations require random testing for drugs and/or alcohol
  • Must pass all required assessments
  • Strict disciplinary policy regarding inability to report to work within proper time limit
  • Advance to engineer position when required, based on seniority
  • This position is governed by a collective bargaining agreement and membership is required
  • Cover outlying locations based on seniority
  • Information about benefits can be found here

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to mount and dismount moving equipment
  • Stoop/bend/kneel/crouch/crawl/balance/climb
  • Work in cramped, confined, enclosed, or awkward places
  • Ride on the outside of rail equipment for extended periods of time
  • Walk long distances over uneven terrain for extended periods of time during shifts
  • Demonstrate auditory and visual acuity/tracking/inspection
  • Must meet color vision and hearing requirements as described in FRA Regulations
  • Frequent lifting up to 80 pounds

Basic Competencies

  • Verbal comprehension (Understand oral and written communications)
  • Communication skills (provide clear instructions/directions)
  • Reasoning skills (problem solving and troubleshooting skills)

Who is Grant Thornton?

At Grant Thornton, we believe in making business more personal and building trust into every result – for our clients and you. Here, we go beyond your expectations of a career in professional services by offering a career path with more: more opportunity, more flexibility, and more support. In the U.S., Grant Thornton delivers professional services through two specialized entities: Grant Thornton LLP, a licensed, certified public accounting (CPA) firm that provides audit and assurance services ― and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (not a licensed CPA firm), which exclusively provides non-attest offerings, including tax and advisory services.

In 2025, Grant Thornton formed a multinational, multidisciplinary platform with Grant Thornton Ireland. The platform offers a premier Trans-Atlantic advisory and tax practice, as well as independent American and Irish audit practices. With $2.7 billion in revenues and more than 50 offices spanning the U.S., Ireland and other territories, the platform delivers a singular client experience that includes enhanced solutions and capabilities, backed by powerful technologies and a roster of 12,000 quality-driven professionals enjoying exceptional career-growth opportunities and a distinctive cross-border culture.

Grant Thornton is part of the Grant Thornton International Limited network, which provides access to its member firms in more than 150 global markets.

About Advisory Services

Grant Thornton’s Advisory professionals are progressive thinkers who create, protect, and transform value today, so our clients have the opportunity to thrive and grow. Our advisory practice creates holistic solutions delivered by innovative, curious professionals who bring technical depth and industry insight to our clients.

What is Risk Advisory?

Within our Cyber & Risk Solution Family, Risk Advisory helps organizations grow with confidence by delivering agile, technology-enabled risk services that strengthen resilience, improve business performance, and unlock new opportunities. We work with complex organizations to assess, transform, and operate internal controls, risk management, compliance and Internal Audit activities, programs, and functions.

POSITION SUMMARY:

Risk Advisory Interns are responsible for working on client engagements, including:

  • Assessing business and information technology processes and system internal controls.
  • Executing enterprise, operational, information technology and third-party risk management and compliance programs.
  • Executing internal audit plans, including information technology internal audits.

A Risk Advisory Intern will gain exposure to various industries, business processes, operations, systems and controls as an integral member of project delivery teams. As a Risk Advisory Intern, you will be executing high quality Risk Advisory projects and services under the supervision of experienced Risk Advisory team members. You will be responsible for efficiently managing your workload to budget and timeline.

title: Director of Data Science & Analytics
description:
Clean luxury. Better for you. At Everlane, we believe luxury should be as effortless as it is conscious. We partner with ethical factories, work with premium, sustainably sourced materials, and strive to leave the industry cleaner than we found it. There's still much to do, and we're excited to grow a team of motivated humans ready for the challenge. The journey toward better continues.

Everlane is seeking a Director of Data Science & Analytics to join our team, where you’ll help drive growth of the Everlane business by leading a team that collaborates with business partners to provide meaningful insights and analysis for critical business decisions, develops reporting, analytics and predictive models, and builds the next generation of Everlane’s data infrastructure. The subject areas that you will impact span the entire company, from analyzing performance marketing data for optimization and helping our digital product team evaluate new opportunities of improvement on our website, to building a model around the purchase preferences of our customers. This position reports into the VP of Digital.

Our team is tasked with building actionable insights from our data, building predictive data products, and creating self-service analytical tools for teams throughout the company. We use a full-stack set of methodologies to achieve this, taking a data science problem from the initial open ended business question, to the eventual productionisation and implementation of a model.

  • Effectively communicate and drive collaboration with key stakeholders across the business to provide insights, analysis and recommendations
  • Own the Data architecture and roadmap, working independently to understand, prioritize, and plan the team’s work
  • Research and promote opportunities to take on new technologies, frameworks, and approaches in customer data analysis, AB testing, data and machine learning
  • Apply causal research and explanatory modeling to better understand customer behavior, marketing performance, site behavior, etc.
  • Deploy predictive data models that our customers will interact with, including product recommendations, size predictions, and predicted return rates
  • Design and analyze rigorous experiments aimed at understanding customer behavior
  • Scale the Everlane data platform with smarter and more sophisticated data on ongoing basis
  • Oversee a skilled team of data analysts, data scientists, and data engineers, coaching direct reports and developing their skills

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • BA/BS degree in business analysis, quantitative or computing focused degree
  • 7+ years of experience in retail/e-commerce or a B2C technology company
  • 5+ years of data technology experience (data collection, analysis, machine learning, statistical modeling)
  • 3+ years of people management experience
  • Ability to understand and interpret the business and provide a firm point of view from both a stakeholder and data perspective
  • Expertise in R, Python, or another data science suitable language

title: Leasing Consultant
description:
We have a fantastic Leasing Consultant opportunity available! $1,500 Sign On Bonus

Weinstein Properties, headquartered in Richmond, Virginia owns and manages over 60 apartment communities in Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Who You Are:

  • Strong Communication Skills: You're a great listener, and you can confidently and warmly connect with others, both in person and in writing.
  • Customer-First Mindset: You love helping people and solving problems, even when things get tough.
  • Positive Energy: You show up with enthusiasm and a can-do attitude — every day, no matter what ends up being thrown your way.

  • Adaptability: You can manage interruptions, shifting priorities, and fast-paced days with ease and grace.

What You Should Know Before You Start:

  • We have high expectations — and a hands-on training program that will set you up to meet them.

Everyone does a little bit of everything.

  • This job is about more than just sales – you will be expected to handle administrative tasks, address resident concerns, and help with property appearance. Everyone does a little bit of everything.

Why Weinstein?

  • Industry-Leading Training: We’ll equip you with all the tools and knowledge you need to grow — no experience necessary.

Ready to join a team that believes in your potential?
Apply today and start building your future with WP.

Initially you will be assigned to one station but will need to be flexible and open to working additional stations as business needs require.   • Operate simple machinery such as automatic Press machines.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to use basic shop math and measurement tools such as tape measures.
  • Ability to follow standard work instructions, assembly drawings, and specifications.
  • Knowledge and ability to use air impact tools and other hand-held tools.

Preferred:

  • Previous experience in an assembly or manufacturing environment a plus.

Physical demands:

  • Standing: All tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
  • Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
  • Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances (less than 1/8 mile).
  • Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
  • Pushing: Occasional pushing of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
  • Pulling: Occasional pulling of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
  • Bending: Frequent bending and crouching to safely lift parts of various sizes and shapes.
  • Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
  • Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
  • Other: Respirator certification required.

title: Silicon Debug Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for solving the hardest problems in silicon? Do you thrive at the intersection of circuit theory, device physics, and hands-on failure investigation? As part of our Silicon Debug group, you'll take complex, often elusive silicon failures and systematically uncover their root cause — from electrical characterization all the way down to physical analysis. You and your team will apply deep engineering fundamentals and cutting-edge failure analysis techniques to enable product ramp at scale. Your efforts will directly impact the quality and reliability of state-of-the-art ASICs that power experiences for millions of customers worldwide. Join us, and you'll play a central role in ensuring the silicon we build is everything it needs to be.

We have an extraordinary opportunity for Silicon Debug Engineers to investigate and root-cause failures in advanced custom digital megacells (SRAM memories, on-chip sensors, custom data paths) used in high-performance, low-power SoCs. You will bridge the gap between electrical debug and physical failure analysis, working at the frontier of silicon investigation.

Imagine yourself at the center of our SoC bring-up and product ramp effort, collaborating across circuit design, process engineering, DFT, and failure analysis teams — with a critical impact on getting functional products to millions of customers quickly.

Minimum Qualifications

  • A minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant field and a minimum of 10 years of relevant industry experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in one or more of the following areas: SRAM circuits, custom circuit design, silicon debug.
  • Experience in design or debug of low-voltage / low-power custom circuits.
  • Deep understanding of deep-submicron device physics, leakage mechanisms, and technology interactions with device behavior.
  • Solid understanding of device matching, device noise sources (1/f, thermal), extrinsic noise sources (supply noise, jitter), and their impact on high-precision circuits.
  • Familiarity with electrical failure analysis (eFA) techniques and physical failure analysis (pFA) workflows, and the ability to plan FA strategies based on electrical debug data.
  • Understanding of Dynamic Lock-in Thermography (DLS) and Lock-in Thermography (LIT) for localization of resistive and leakage defects, including their sensitivity limits and how thermal signatures correlate to specific circuit fault modes.
  • Knowledge of Nanoprobe techniques for electrical probing of deep-submicron nodes, and appreciation of how probe contact, voltage bias, and electron beam exposure can perturb sensitive analog or memory circuits.
  • Awareness of how physical sample preparation steps (deprocessing, FIB cross-section, delayering) can alter or destroy evidence of electrical failures, and how to coordinate FA plans that preserve failure signatures.
  • Ability to interpret FA results (photon emission maps, OBIRCH, thermal maps, TEM/SEM imagery) in the context of circuit topology and failure electrical signatures.
  • Ability to conduct structured experiments during silicon debug, gather and analyze large datasets, and utilize scripting to support efficient handling of debug data.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Perl, or others) and CAD automation tools.
  • Knowledge of industry-standard circuit design and simulation tools.

title: Oracle Fusion ERP Technical Analyst
description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

We are looking for a seasoned Oracle Fusion ERP Technical Analyst to join our Financial Systems team and accelerate a portfolio of Order-to-Cash (O2C), Record-to-Report (R2R) and Procure to Pay (P2P) transformation initiatives. In this role you will own the design, development, and delivery of custom reports, data integration interfaces, document templates, and REST/SOAP API solutions within Oracle Fusion Cloud — enabling finance and cross-functional stakeholders to operate with greater speed and accuracy.

The Financial Systems team owns the technology backbone for Instacart's finance operations, managing Oracle Fusion, Zip, Billing Platform, OIC, HighRadius, Workiva, and FloQast. We partner closely with Finance, Platform Engineering, and the CTO organization to drive transformation initiatives that scale with the business. You'll work on meaningful projects, see your contributions in production quickly, and have a direct line to executive stakeholders.

What you'll cook up in your first year

Reporting & Analytics

  • Finance reporting requirements are met through a production-ready Oracle BIP library: data models, RTF templates, and scheduled bursting jobs are built and maintained, and parameterized BIP reports are exposed as REST endpoints for programmatic access by external systems and dashboards.
  • Business Intelligence Cloud Connector (BICC) extracts are configured and maintained for data warehouse integration and downstream analytics, giving finance stakeholders scalable, reusable access to financial data.

Document Customization

  • External-facing document templates, including Invoices, Credit Memos, Statements, and Purchase Orders, are designed and customized using RTF and XML Publisher, with corporate branding, conditional logic, and dynamic data sections applied to meet audit and customer experience standards.
  • Sub-templates and style templates are built and maintained to enforce consistent formatting across the full document library, reducing one-off customization work.

Data Integration & FBDI

  • File-Based Data Import (FBDI) templates and automation scripts are production-ready for bulk data loads across AR, AP, GL, and other Fusion modules, and inbound/outbound interface files (CSV, XML, JSON) are built and maintained for integrations with billing platforms, collections tools, and third-party financial applications, with load errors troubleshot, data mappings validated, and interface specs documented.

API & Systems Integration

  • REST and SOAP API integrations are live between Oracle Fusion and systems including Billing Platform, HighRadius, Workiva, and FloQast, designed and implemented using Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and BIP-generated endpoints, with reusable integration patterns for inbound and outbound data flows aligned to CTO org architecture and API governance standards.

Transformation Project Support

  • O2C, R2R, and P2P transformation workstreams have clear technical specifications, with solutions documented in Confluence, development tasks tracked in Jira, and accurate status updates delivered to executive stakeholders through steerco and roadmap planning cycles.




The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

  • 5+ years of hands-on Oracle Fusion Cloud technical development experience.
  • Deep expertise in Oracle BIP: data models, RTF templates, XML Publisher, parameter-driven reports, and bursting.
  • Proven experience building FBDI templates across multiple Fusion modules (AR, AP, GL, FA, or similar).
  • Strong BICC configuration and data extraction experience for analytics and data warehouse use cases.
  • Experience designing and customizing Oracle Fusion invoice templates and other external-facing transactional documents using RTF and XML.
  • Proficiency with XML, XSLT, and XPath for document and data transformation.
  • Hands-on experience with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or equivalent middleware for REST/SOAP API development.
  • Strong written communication skills — comfortable producing technical specs, interface docs, and steerco-ready summaries.

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Oracle Fusion Cloud certification (Technical or Financials track).
  • Experience integrating Oracle Fusion with Workday, HighRadius, Workiva, FloQast, or billing/collections platforms.
  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks and solution design documentation.
  • Exposure to BI Catalog management and OTBI reporting.
  • Experience with Oracle Smart View for Office for ad-hoc financial analysis and reporting.
  • Knowledge of Oracle Financial Reporting Studio (FRS) for building formatted financial statements.
  • Familiarity with Financial Data Integration (FDI) for managing data load rules, mappings, and data management workflows (nice to have).
  • Exposure to Oracle Visual Builder Cloud Service (VBCS) for building lightweight web UIs or extending Oracle Fusion applications.
  • Experience in a high-growth, fast-paced technology company.
  • Prior involvement in large-scale ERP transformation, module implementation, or re-platforming projects.

title: Graduate Research Associate, Clinical Outcomes
location: South San Francisco, CA, United States
description:
Overview (Why This Role?)
Hearst Health is seeking a part-time Graduate Research Associate, Clinical Outcomes to help quantify and communicate the clinical impact of our software, data, and decision-support solutions.
This role is designed for a student pursuing an advanced degree in public health, health services research, epidemiology, biostatistics, health informatics, or a related field who wants to apply rigorous research methods to real-world healthcare questions.
The core question behind the role is straightforward but important: Do patients and healthcare organizations achieve better clinical outcomes when they use Hearst Health solutions?
Working with Hearst Health leadership and the Chief Medical Officers and clinical leaders across our businesses, the Graduate Research Associate will help turn that question into testable hypotheses, design appropriate analyses, evaluate real-world data, and develop credible evidence about the relationship between use of our solutions and clinical outcomes.
This is not primarily an academic research role. The objective is to produce rigorous, defensible evidence that can inform product strategy and, where supported by the findings, strengthen how Hearst Health communicates the value of its solutions to customers and the market.
The position is expected to require approximately 10–20 hours per week, with flexibility to accommodate an academic schedule.
Compensation: $50 an hour
This position is eligible for Remote Work.
About Hearst Health
The mission of Hearst Health is to guide healthcare organizations by delivering essential intelligence and software that improve the quality, safety and efficiency of care. Hearst Health has been innovating with care for more than 40 years, with a commitment to making a lasting positive impact on health. The Hearst Health companies — FDB, Homecare Homebase, MCG, MHK, QGenda and Zynx Health — elevate care by informing and empowering participants across the health journey. To learn more, follow @Hearst-Health on LinkedIn.
Key Responsibilities
Clinical Outcomes Research & Study Design
  • Partner with Chief Medical Officers, clinical leaders, product teams, and other stakeholders across Hearst Health businesses to identify high-value questions about the clinical impact of our solutions.
  • Translate business and clinical questions into testable hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and well-defined research designs.
  • Develop appropriate observational, quasi-experimental, or other analytical approaches to assess whether and how clinical outcomes change following adoption or use of Hearst Health solutions.
  • Identify relevant endpoints, comparison populations, time periods, covariates, and potential confounding factors.
  • Assess the strengths and limitations of available data and recommend pragmatic study designs that balance methodological rigor with real-world constraints.
Data Analysis & Evidence Development
  • Analyze clinical, operational, utilization, or other relevant healthcare data to evaluate outcomes associated with Hearst Health solutions.
  • Apply appropriate statistical and epidemiological methods to distinguish meaningful effects from correlation, selection effects, and other sources of bias.
  • Conduct sensitivity analyses and other validation work to assess the robustness of findings.
  • Document methodology, assumptions, limitations, and results so analyses can withstand scrutiny from clinical, analytical, and customer audiences.
  • Where an analysis does not demonstrate a meaningful clinical benefit, clearly characterize the result and help identify what should be tested or investigated next.
Insight Translation & Communication
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear conclusions for clinical and business audiences.
  • Develop charts, exhibits, research summaries, and other materials that explain study methodology and findings accurately and accessibly.
  • Partner with marketing, sales, product, and clinical teams to determine how validated findings can appropriately support customer conversations, case studies, thought leadership, and other external communications.
  • Help ensure that claims about clinical impact remain consistent with the underlying evidence and appropriately reflect study limitations.
Research Portfolio Development
  • Help establish a repeatable framework for measuring clinical impact across Hearst Health businesses and products.
  • Identify opportunities to extend initial analyses into deeper research, customer-specific studies, conference submissions, white papers, or peer-reviewed research where appropriate.
  • Monitor relevant academic literature and emerging methodologies for evaluating digital health, clinical decision support, healthcare software, and data products.
What Success Looks Like
  • Rigorous evidence: Research questions are translated into credible study designs and analyses that can withstand clinical and methodological scrutiny.
  • Decision-useful findings: Analyses produce clear answers—including negative or inconclusive results—that help Hearst Health understand where its solutions have measurable impact.
  • Clinical credibility: Chief Medical Officers and other clinical leaders view the Associate as a capable research partner who understands both methodological rigor and real-world healthcare.
  • Commercial relevance: Validated findings can be translated into clear, evidence-based insights that strengthen customer and market conversations without overstating what the research demonstrates.
  • Repeatability: The work contributes to a scalable approach for measuring clinical impact across multiple Hearst Health businesses and solutions.
Qualifications (What We're Looking For)
Must-Have Qualifications
  • Currently pursuing an advanced degree—such as an MPH, MS, DrPH, PhD, or comparable graduate degree—in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, health services research, health informatics, outcomes research, or a related quantitative field.
  • Strong grounding in research methodology, epidemiology, biostatistics, or causal inference.
  • Experience designing and conducting quantitative analyses using healthcare, clinical, claims, EHR, or other complex real-world datasets.
  • Proficiency with at least one statistical or analytical programming environment.
  • Ability to move from an open-ended clinical question to a structured research plan and analytical approach.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical findings to non-technical audiences.
  • Intellectual curiosity and comfort working across clinical, analytical, product, and commercial perspectives.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with observational or quasi-experimental methods used in real-world evidence generation, such as propensity score methods, matched cohort designs, difference-in-differences, interrupted time series, or related approaches.
  • Familiarity with healthcare quality measures, clinical outcomes, utilization measures, or healthcare economics.
  • Experience working with claims, EHR, clinical workflow, or other healthcare datasets.
  • Prior research experience resulting in a publication, poster, conference presentation, thesis, or similar research output.
  • Interest in healthcare technology and in understanding how software, information, and clinical decision-support tools affect care delivery and patient outcomes.

title: Program and Logistics Management, Senior F-16 WAM (Secret) - 190
location: Hill Air Force Base, Utah, United States
description:
Overview

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With more than 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI & data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver on a scale and with purpose.

We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by The Washington Post for six consecutive years and named to the Inc. 5000 list of Fastest-Growing Private Companies in 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming environment for those looking to grow and make a meaningful impact. We encourage employees to push boundaries and help solve critical, world-changing federal challenges.

Position Summary

Credence has an immediate opening for a Program and Logistics Management who will be primarily responsible for supporting the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center WAM (AFLCMC/WAM) directorate, F-16 division at Hill AFB, UT.

F-16 “Viper” AFLCMC/WAM is headquartered at Hill Air Force Base with units located at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Tyndall Air Force Base, Eglin Air Force Base, and Davis-Monthan Air Force Base. The F-16 “Viper” is a multi-role fighter jet delivering air-to-air, air-to-ground, and surveillance capabilities for the United States Air Force (USAF) and Coalition Partners.

The F-16 program has the largest Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program in U.S. history producing over 4,500 jets for 24 countries. Each F-16 FMS case is uniquely tailored to country requirements / development / funding. Presently, FMS production orders exist through 2030. Additionally, the F-16 program includes the Multi-National Fighter Program (MNFP). MNFP is not a typical FMS program, but a unique, cooperative USAF and development program implemented through the FMS process under the framework of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). MNFP began in 1975 with the countries of Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Norway; Portugal joined in 200.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the duties listed below:

  • Provide program management and logistics management support to the F-16 structural, mechanical and avionics systems. The Contractor shall assist to prepare documents, create, and establish plans to include an IMS of events identifying and streamlining the overall program implementation with IPT membership coordination. The schedules shall include all actions required to monitor and track program milestones and timelines, track all program deliverables, create and implement corrective action plans to maintain schedule and cost while supporting program requirements, and conduct budget planning/budget submissions.
  • Assist to interface with appropriate weapon system Contractors and DoD agencies to support the program.
  • Support the preparation and review of pertinent data, coordinate with applicable managers, and finalize related documentation/information for verbal presentation of the program status at required meetings.
  • Support IPT meetings, flight test requirements, PMRs, technical interface meetings, kit and technical order validations, conferences, and others as required.
  • Support related engineering and logistics tasks and functions related to program development and integration.
  • Assist to ensure spares provisioning is accomplished on all items to support program requirements and shall interface with appropriate program and/or item managers, modification managers and equipment specialists at both Contractor and DoD agencies.
  • Ensure that F-16 spares requirements are identified and shall support the coordination of programming the requisite funding to meet the requirements.
  • Support development of requirements documents to support acquisition and sustainment efforts.
  • Support PMRs and assist with the completion of risk assessments and proposal and implementation of mitigation solutions.
  • Support and coordinate programming requisite funding for the overall program requirements for support equipment, Contractor data, testing reports, hardware, training, and outside engineering support.
  • Assist in the development, implementation and maintenance of integrated logistics management plans.
  • Assist to develop and apply maintenance concepts including necessary depot support.
  • Assist to identify and support Source of Repair Assignment Process (SORAP) requirements and actions; manage Reliability Centered Maintenance Analysis (RCMA); manage provisioning planning and implementation; and support F-16 sustaining engineers as required.
  • Support the management of life cycle logistics planning to include end-of-program requirements and life cycle cost development.

Requirements

  • Minimum of an active Secret security clearance.
  • Master’s or Doctoral Degree in a related field and a minimum of ten (10) years of experience in the respective technical / professional discipline being performed, at least five (5) of which must be in the DoD
  • OR, Bachelor’s Degree in a related field and a minimum of twelve (12) years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed, five (5) of which must be in the DoD
  • OR, a minimum of fifteen (15) years of directly related experience with proper certifications as described in the PWS labor category performance requirements, eight (8) of which must be in the DoD

Why This Role Matters

  • Real-World Impact — Your work will support defense and health agencies where AI solutions directly contribute to national security and public well-being.
  • Growth-Oriented Environment — Learn from technical leaders, innovate within Agentic AI, and mentor those around you in AI best practices.

title: Programme Analyst, Gender, NOA, FTA, La Havana, Cuba
description:
The Position:

The Programme Analyst, Gender (NOA) at UNFPA Cuba is responsible for the management, coordination, and technical implementation of the project "Supporting the National Response to Gender-Based Violence in Cuba", signed in March 2024 and funded by the Government of Canada. In close partnership with the Federation of Cuban Women (FMC) and other key sectors (health, legal, law enforcement, and social-community), the position leads capacity-building efforts at both national and local levels to ensure a comprehensive, integrated, and survivor-centered response to gender-based violence.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person's potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The Programme Analyst, Gender is located in the UNFPA CUBA Country Office (CO) and reports to the Head of Office. The incumbent works closely with other programme and operations officers and contributes strategic guidance to ensure efficient, effective, and timely design and delivery of UNFPA CO’s country programme results and provides high-level technical assistance, promotes gender equality and human rights frameworks, and ensures that project monitoring, evaluation, and results-based reporting strictly aligns with both UNFPA's standards and donor´s requirements.

You would be responsible for:

1. Technical Leadership and Programmatic Oversight

  • Territorial Coordination and Implementation: Plan, coordinate, and technically monitor project activities across the 40 selected pilot municipalities in the country's 15 provinces.
  • Deconstruction of Social Norms: Design, supervise, and evaluate communication, awareness-raising, and advocacy strategies aimed at transforming gender stereotypes, social norms, and discriminatory patriarchal practices at local and national levels.
  • Strengthening of Essential Services: Facilitate the creation, equipment, and strengthening of integrated, coordinated response services (health, legal, law enforcement, and social-community) for survivors of gender-based violence, leveraging the established capacities of the FMC's Women and Family Guidance Centers and other local spaces.

2. Capacity Building and Strategic Partnerships

  • Technical Assistance to Counterparts: Provide high-level technical advice and strengthen the capacities of the Federation of Cuban Women (FMC) as the lead national counterpart, as well as other key institutional sectors (health, justice, law enforcement, media/communicators, and community actors).
  • Management of Specialists and Protocols: Coordinate with local gender and GBV specialists and consultants to develop methodological tools, training programs, and the standardization of multi-sectoral protocols.

3. Monitoring, Reporting, and Results-Based Management (RBM)

  • Quality Assurance and RBM: Ensure that operational planning (Annual Work Plans - AWPs) and activity implementation are carried out under the Results-Based Management (RBM) approach, with a rigorous gender equality and human rights perspective.
  • Donor Reporting: Prepare high-quality, technical annual and final results-based narrative reports on project progress, indicators, challenges, lessons learned, and sustainability, strictly complying with the deadlines and quality standards of Global Affairs Canada (GAC).
  • Systematization and Policy Advocacy: Systematize lessons learned from municipal pilot experiences to provide inputs that directly feed back into the implementation of the National Comprehensive Strategy for the Prevention and Care of Gender-Based Violence and Family Violence, as well as the National Program for the Advancement of Women (PAM).

4. Partnership and Advocacy

  • Coordinating the Advocacy/Gender component project activities and ensuring their timely implementation.
  • Fostering an effective working relationship with NGOs whose activities focus on Women’s health, status and gender related issues, strengthening the women NGO network.
  • Planning the project activities with relevant partners including budgetary requirements and logistics arrangements.
  • Coordinating organization of meetings, workshops and training. Preparing relevant documentation including background documents, meeting and expenditure reports.
  • Assisting UNFPA and other partners in organizing meetings, training briefing sessions.
  • Acting as the focal point for development of project documents and concept papers on gender issues for external (non-core) funding.
  • Assisting the Head of Office for the various projects on gender issues implemented by UNFPA.
  • Representing UNFPA CUBA in the Gender Interagency Group.
  • Establishing a close working relationship with the Gender related Parliamentary Committees to secure the involvement of influential people and the private sector representatives in population and gender activities.
  • Participating in advocacy task groups of the UNFPA CO to provide input into all advocacy related activities.

Carrying out other tasks as appropriate and required.

Qualifications and Experience:

Education:

Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Law, Public Policy, Public Administration, or other related fields relevant to the UNFPA mandate with emphasis on Gender and Gender Based Violence

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Progressively relevant experience in project coordination and/or research on areas related to Gender and Gender Based Violence.
  • Background in planning and reporting work experience at the UN System will be considered an advantage.
  • Excellent writing and oral communication skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills.
  • Advanced computer skills are necessary.

Languages:

Fluency in Spanish is required. English working knowledge is required.

Required Competencies:

Values:

  • Exemplifying integrity,
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,
  • Embracing cultural diversity,
  • Embracing change

Core Competencies:

  • Achieving results,
  • Being accountable,
  • Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,
  • Thinking analytically and strategically,
  • Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,
  • Communicating for impact.

Functional Competencies:

  • Advocacy/advancing a policy-oriented agenda.
  • Leveraging the resources of national governments and partners/building strategic alliances & partnerships.
  • Delivering Results Based Programmes.
  • Creating visibility for the organization.

title: Soldering Technician
description:
West Coast Magnetics | Stockton, CA | $20.93–$27.00/hour

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.

West Coast Magnetics is a fast-growing, close-knit manufacturer specializing in custom electronic assemblies for the medical, aerospace, semiconductor, communications, and test & measurement industries. When off-the-shelf parts won't cut it, our team engineers the solution - and skilled soldering technicians are at the heart of how we make that happen.

We're looking for a Soldering Technician who takes pride in precise, repeatable, high-quality work and wants to build complex coils, transformers, and assemblies that go into critical, high-performance applications.

Why Soldering Experience Matters Here

This isn't high-volume, low-complexity assembly. Our work is high-mix, high-complexity, which means:

  • You'll solder intricate coil and transformer assemblies where accuracy and consistency are non-negotiable
  • Every joint and connection needs to meet exacting quality standards - the first time, every time
  • You'll read and interpret detailed work instructions and translate them into flawless finished products
  • Your solder work directly supports mission-critical industries like aerospace, medical devices, and semiconductor manufacturing

If you already have soldering experience, you'll fit right in. Steady hands, attention to detail, and a genuine understanding of solder technique are what set our technicians apart.

What You'll Do

  • Build complex coils and assemblies from start to finish with high levels of quality and repeatability
  • Solder, tin, strip, cut wire, wind, glue, coat, and varnish as required by the job
  • Inspect your own work to ensure 100% accuracy and compliance with work instructions
  • Document first article builds and pre-runs with clear, detailed notes
  • Test complex coils and transformers
  • Keep safety front and center, following all safety rules and procedures
  • Work efficiently without sacrificing quality
  • Maintain a clean, organized workspace
  • Collaborate well with your supervisor and teammates

What You Bring

  • Soldering experience strongly preferred - comfort and skill with a soldering iron is central to this role
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Basic math and reading skills
  • Ability to read and follow detailed technical work instructions
  • A quality-first mindset and pride in getting the job right the first time

What We Offer

  • Competitive pay: $20.93–$27.00/hour
  • 401(k) with company matching
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Referral program
  • A genuine small-company culture where your work - and your craftsmanship - is noticed and valued

About West Coast Magnetics

We're not a company that settles for "standard." When our customers need something that doesn't exist yet, we engineer it. Our teams design, manufacture, and test custom electronic assemblies for some of the most demanding industries out there. If you want your soldering skills to matter and your work to end up in products that push boundaries, we'd love to meet you.

Ready to put your soldering skills to work? Apply today and join a team that builds what others can't.

West Coast Magnetics is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

title: Sr Lead Software Engineer - Platform Engineering
description:
Be an integral part of an agile team that's constantly pushing the envelope to enhance, build, and deliver top-notch technology products.
As a Sr Lead Software Engineer - Platform Engineering at JPMorgan Chase within the Commercial & Investment Bank - Payments Technology Space, you are an integral part of an agile team that works to enhance, build, and deliver trusted market-leading technology products in a secure, stable, and scalable way. Drive significant business impact through your capabilities and contributions, and apply deep technical expertise and problem-solving methodologies to tackle a diverse array of challenges that span multiple technologies and applications.
Job responsibilities
  • Design, build, and maintain a proprietary Java framework built on Spring Boot — starters, auto-configuration, dependency management, and integration with standard libraries for messaging, data, and observability
  • Own and evolve the framework versioning and release strategy — supporting multiple active major versions simultaneously while managing consumer migrations deliberately
  • Build and maintain the test automation strategy for the framework: unit, integration, and contract tests that give the team confidence that changes are safe before they reach the ~1,000+ application teams that consume each release
  • Conduct rigorous, high-quality PR reviews — explaining the why behind feedback, raising the technical standard of the local team through the review process
  • Own the team's approach to containerized delivery — including framework integration with managed container images, container runtime behavior, and how the framework layer interacts with the platform's image strategy
  • Contribute to shared platform services — the running services that the framework wires applications into at runtime; understanding the full build-to-runtime picture is essential
  • Drives team adoption of enterprise-authorized AI-assisted engineering practices within the work environment to improve code quality, delivery speed, and operational outcomes (e.g., AI-assisted code review/refactoring, test strategy acceleration, incident/root-cause analysis support), while establishing consistent validation standards (secure coding, peer review, automated testing) and promoting reuse of effective patterns across the team
  • Applies knowledge of tools within the Software Development Life Cycle toolchain, including enterprise-authorized AI-assisted development and automation capabilities, to improve the value realized by automation
  • Actively participate in global platform design discussions with counterparts in other locations, representing Austin's perspective and contributing to cross-site architectural decisions
  • Diagnose and resolve complex, cross-cutting issues where root cause is in the framework layer rather than in any individual consumer application
  • Apply system design principles to framework and platform problems — making and clearly communicating critical design decisions with long-lived consequences

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
  • Formal training or certification on software engineering concepts and 5+ years applied experience
  • Significant Java engineering experience with demonstrable depth in framework or platform library development — candidates should be able to speak to versioning, compatibility, and testing challenges specific to shared library work
  • Strong understanding of Spring Boot internals — auto-configuration, condition evaluation, bean lifecycle, and how framework code interacts with application context
  • Experience building and maintaining test automation for library/framework code, including integration test harnesses that exercise real downstream behavior
  • Understanding of semantic versioning, backward compatibility contracts, and multi-version support strategies — ability to reason about what constitutes a breaking change and manage consumers through one
  • Solid experience with containerized applications and container runtime systems — including managed container image strategies, image layering, runtime concerns (JVM/GC arguments, sidecar patterns), and how framework choices affect container behavior
  • Demonstrated experience leading effective use of approved AI-assisted software development tools (e.g., for coding, code review, test acceleration, troubleshooting) with the ability to set team expectations for validating AI outputs for correctness, performance, and security
  • Strong understanding of responsible AI use in engineering workflows, including data sensitivity considerations, secure handling of inputs/outputs, and adherence to resiliency and security expectations; experience coaching engineers on safe, compliant adoption within delivery practices
  • Hands-on experience with core cloud CI/CD tooling — including infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and deployment pipeline tooling (Spinnaker); understanding of how platform software is built, versioned, and deployed in a cloud-native environment
  • Strong system design skills with the ability to demonstrate critical thinking on architectural trade-offs — particularly decisions that affect a large consumer base over multiple years
  • Proven track record as a technical lead — mentoring engineers, conducting substantive code reviews, and raising the quality of a team's output, not just individual output

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Experience with Kafka, Cassandra, or OpenTelemetry instrumentation at the framework/starter level
  • Prior experience building or maintaining an internal Java framework built on Spring Boot, or equivalent proprietary platform library in a large organization
  • Experience in a large-scale engineering organization — where decisions affect many teams, migrations require coordination at scale, and platform stability is a hard constraint
  • Background in financial services — understanding of the regulatory, audit, and controls environment that shapes how platform software is built and operated in a bank
  • Experience working across geographically distributed teams in a senior or lead capacity
